purpose: Verified route seed for Garda Citizen Access. This site guides citizens to official processes and does not itself submit complaints, reports, applications or requests.
verification_note: Only routes with current official-source evidence are seeded here; conflicting or incomplete routes remain explicitly flagged.

routes.citizen_question: Emergency / immediate danger
routes.notes: 999 or 112; do not wait for an online form.
routes.purpose_plain: Get an immediate emergency Garda response.
routes.eligibility: Anyone who needs an emergency Garda response in Ireland.
routes.emergency_rule: Emergency route itself; do not wait for an online form.
routes.next_steps: Follow the emergency operator's instructions.

routes.citizen_question: I was directly affected by, or directly witnessed, Garda behaviour
routes.notes: Fiosrú determines admissibility; a Garda name is not required.
routes.purpose_plain: Make a formal complaint about Garda personnel through the statutory complaints system.
routes.eligibility: Initial screening asks whether the person was directly affected or directly witnessed the Garda behaviour; Fiosrú determines admissibility.
routes.deadline: Normally within 12 months; a late complaint may be considered where Fiosrú accepts there is good reason for the delay.
routes.next_steps: Fiosrú assesses admissibility; if admitted, the complaint may be resolved by Garda or investigated by Fiosrú depending on the statutory route.
routes.conflict_note: Fiosrú's current submission page warns that knowingly false or misleading information is a criminal offence under s.226 and explains that complaint information may be shared in specified circumstances.

routes.citizen_question: I need to report a non-emergency crime
routes.notes: Use a Garda station when no specialist online route fits.
routes.purpose_plain: Report a non-emergency crime to Gardaí.
routes.eligibility: Use when the matter falls within Garda jurisdiction and no more specific current online route is appropriate.
routes.emergency_rule: Immediate danger, crime in progress, serious injury risk or offender at/near scene → 999/112.
routes.next_steps: Garda records and assesses the report and may investigate.

routes.citizen_question: I need to report a qualifying theft online
routes.notes: Current online theft declaration is for property not exceeding €1,000 in Ireland.
routes.purpose_plain: Submit the current online theft declaration where its conditions are met.
routes.eligibility: Current online declaration is for theft of property not exceeding €1,000 in Ireland.
routes.emergency_rule: Do not use for emergencies or categories excluded by current Garda guidance.
routes.geographic_scope: Ireland excluding Northern Ireland for the current online theft declaration
routes.next_steps: Provide requested details; current form warns that the submission cannot be edited after submission.

routes.citizen_question: I want to report a non-emergency traffic incident
routes.notes: Current form says reports should generally be within 6 months.
routes.purpose_plain: Report a qualifying non-emergency road-traffic incident through Traffic Watch.
routes.eligibility: Non-emergency traffic matter meeting current Traffic Watch conditions.
routes.deadline: Current Traffic Watch form states reports should generally be made within 6 months.
routes.next_steps: Garda reviews the report; an investigator may contact the reporter and request a statement.

routes.citizen_question: I want to report a suspected hate crime or hate incident
routes.notes: Emergency → 999/112.
routes.purpose_plain: Report a suspected hate crime or hate incident.
routes.eligibility: Non-emergency suspected hate crime/hate incident.
routes.next_steps: Garda assesses and responds under its hate-crime procedures.

routes.citizen_question: I want to give confidential information about crime or other activity
routes.notes: Garda Confidential: 1800 666 111.
routes.purpose_plain: Provide information confidentially to Gardaí.
routes.eligibility: People wishing to provide relevant confidential information.
routes.next_steps: Garda receives and assesses the information.

routes.citizen_question: I want to access personal data Gardaí hold about me
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána Data Protection Unit
routes.notes: F20/data-protection access route; subject to applicable law.
routes.purpose_plain: Exercise the applicable data-protection access right using the Garda F20 route.
routes.eligibility: Subject to GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018 and applicable exemptions.
routes.next_steps: Garda Data Protection Unit processes the request subject to applicable law.

routes.citizen_question: I want administrative records held by Gardaí
routes.notes: Current Garda sources describe response timing differently; preserve source-specific wording.
routes.purpose_plain: Make an FOI request for records within the FOI regime.
routes.eligibility: Subject to the Freedom of Information Act and exemptions; Garda identifies administrative areas including HR, Finance and Procurement.
routes.geographic_scope: Ireland / Garda records within FOI scope
routes.conflict_note: Current Garda pages describe response timing differently; do not hard-code one universal deadline.
routes.next_steps: Identify the records sought and request access under FOI.

routes.citizen_question: I want environmental information held by Gardaí
routes.notes: AIE is distinct from FOI.
routes.purpose_plain: Request environmental information under the AIE regime.
routes.eligibility: Subject to the AIE Regulations and applicable exceptions.
routes.next_steps: The request is processed under the AIE regime.

routes.citizen_question: I need a Garda Police Certificate for a qualifying purpose
routes.notes: Specific current submission instructions must be verified before activation.
routes.purpose_plain: Apply for a Police Certificate where current qualifying circumstances apply.
routes.eligibility: Specified purposes include certain foreign consular/visa, EU, overseas employment/aid and qualifying overseas study circumstances.
routes.geographic_scope: Republic of Ireland residence/former residence as described by Garda
routes.conflict_note: Broader page mentions online completion while current FAQ specifies postal submission; verify current submission instruction before activation.
routes.next_steps: Complete current application and follow current submission instructions.

routes.citizen_question: An organisation has asked me to complete Garda Vetting
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána National Vetting Bureau
routes.notes: Registered organisation initiates the application.
routes.purpose_plain: Complete an eVetting application initiated by a registered organisation.
routes.eligibility: Applicant must meet current age, identity, email and registered-organisation requirements.
routes.next_steps: The registered organisation initiates the application; applicant completes the invitation process.

routes.citizen_question: I need voluntary proof of age
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána / Age Card service
routes.notes: Voluntary proof-of-age card for people aged 18+.
routes.purpose_plain: Apply for the voluntary National Age Card for proof of age.
routes.eligibility: People aged 18 or over, subject to current application requirements.
routes.next_steps: Apply through the official Age Card service and complete required Garda-station authentication.

routes.citizen_question: I want to see whether recovered property matches something I lost
routes.notes: Search does not replace reporting stolen property.
routes.purpose_plain: Search selected recovered lost/stolen property.
routes.eligibility: Public search of property included in the current pilot.
routes.next_steps: If a matching item is identified, follow Garda instructions; stolen property should still be reported.

routes.citizen_question: I already received a Fixed Charge Notice and want to challenge/cancel it
routes.notes: Must not be presented as a new traffic report.
routes.purpose_plain: Use the official FCN cancellation/review process where applicable.
routes.eligibility: Person who has received an FCN and meets applicable review/cancellation conditions.
routes.next_steps: Use the current cancellation/review instructions for the specific notice.

routes.citizen_question: Gardaí told me they will not prosecute and I want the decision reviewed

routes.citizen_question: Fiosrú has told me my complaint is inadmissible or that its investigation will be discontinued and I want a review.
routes.purpose_plain: Request the statutory review of an Fiosrú inadmissibility or discontinuance decision.
routes.eligibility: The original complainant; sufficient information must be provided to link the request to the original complaint.
routes.emergency_rule: This is a post-decision review, not an emergency route.
routes.contact: review@fiosru.ie; Review Unit, Fiosrú, 150 Upper Abbey Street, Dublin 1, D01 FT73
routes.deadline: Normally within 28 days of being informed of the decision; good reasons for additional time may be considered.
routes.next_steps: Fiosrú's independent review process considers whether the decision was fair, reasonable and proportionate on the available facts.
